In [[mathematics]], the '''coadjoint representation''' <math>K</math> of a [[Lie group]] <math>G</math> is the [[dual representation|dual]] of the [[adjoint representation of a Lie group|adjoint representation]]. If <math>\mathfrak{g}</math> denotes the [[Lie algebra]] of <math>G</math>, the corresponding action of <math>G</math> on <math>\mathfrak{g}^*</math>, the [[dual space]] to <math>\mathfrak{g}</math>, is called the '''coadjoint action'''. A geometrical interpretation is as the action by left-translation on the space of right-invariant [[1-form]]s on <math>G</math>.

The importance of the coadjoint representation was emphasised by work of [[Alexandre Kirillov]], who showed that for [[nilpotent Lie group]]s <math>G</math> a basic role in their [[representation theory]] is played by '''coadjoint orbits'''.
In the Kirillov method of orbits, representations of <math>G</math> are constructed geometrically starting from the coadjoint orbits. In some sense those play a substitute role for the [[conjugacy class]]es of <math>G</math>, which again may be complicated, while the orbits are relatively tractable.

==Formal definition==
Let <math>G</math> be a Lie group and <math>\mathfrak{g}</math> be its Lie algebra. Let <math>\mathrm{Ad} : G \rightarrow \mathrm{Aut}(\mathfrak{g})</math> denote the [[adjoint representation]] of <math>G</math>. Then the '''coadjoint representation''' <math>\mathrm{Ad}^*: G \rightarrow \mathrm{GL}(\mathfrak{g}^*)</math> is defined by
:<math>\langle \mathrm{Ad}^*_g \, \mu, Y \rangle = \langle \mu, \mathrm{Ad}^{-1}_{g} Y \rangle = \langle \mu, \mathrm{Ad}_{g^{-1}} Y \rangle</math> for <math>g \in G, Y \in \mathfrak{g}, \mu \in \mathfrak{g}^*,</math>
where <math>\langle \mu, Y \rangle</math> denotes the value of the linear functional <math>\mu</math> on the vector <math>Y</math>.

Let <math>\mathrm{ad}^*</math> denote the representation of the Lie algebra <math>\mathfrak{g}</math> on <math>\mathfrak{g}^*</math> induced by the coadjoint representation of the Lie group <math>G</math>. Then the infinitesimal version of the defining equation for <math>\mathrm{Ad}^*</math> reads:
:<math>\langle \mathrm{ad}^*_X \mu, Y \rangle = \langle \mu, - \mathrm{ad}_X Y \rangle = - \langle \mu, [X, Y] \rangle</math> for <math>X,Y \in \mathfrak{g}, \mu \in \mathfrak{g}^*</math>

where <math>\mathrm{ad}</math> is the [[adjoint representation of a Lie algebra|adjoint representation of the Lie algebra]] <math>\mathfrak{g}</math>.

==Coadjoint orbit==

A coadjoint orbit <math>\mathcal{O}_\mu</math> for <math>\mu</math> in the dual space <math>\mathfrak{g}^*</math> of <math>\mathfrak{g}</math> may be defined either extrinsically, as the actual [[orbit (group theory)|orbit]] <math>\mathrm{Ad}^*_G \mu</math> inside <math>\mathfrak{g}^*</math>, or intrinsically as the [[homogeneous space]] <math>G/G_\mu</math> where <math>G_\mu</math> is the [[Group action (mathematics)#Orbits and stabilizers|stabilizer]] of <math>\mu</math> with respect to the coadjoint action; this distinction is worth making since the embedding of the orbit may be complicated.

The coadjoint orbits are submanifolds of <math>\mathfrak{g}^*</math> and carry a natural symplectic structure. On each orbit <math>\mathcal{O}_\mu</math>, there is a closed non-degenerate <math>G</math>-invariant [[2-form]] <math>\omega \in \Omega^2(\mathcal{O}_\mu)</math> inherited from <math>\mathfrak{g}</math> in the following manner:

:<math>\omega_\nu(\mathrm{ad}^*_X \nu, \mathrm{ad}^*_Y \nu) := \langle \nu, [X, Y] \rangle , \nu \in \mathcal{O}_\mu, X, Y \in \mathfrak{g}</math>.

The well-definedness, non-degeneracy, and <math>G</math>-invariance of <math>\omega</math> follow from the following facts:

(i) The tangent space <math>\mathrm{T}_\nu \mathcal{O}_\mu = \{ -\mathrm{ad}^*_X \nu : X \in \mathfrak{g}\}</math> may be identified with <math>\mathfrak{g}/\mathfrak{g}_\nu</math>, where <math>\mathfrak{g}_\nu</math> is the Lie algebra of <math>G_\nu</math>.

(ii) The kernel of the map <math>X \mapsto \langle \nu, [X, \cdot] \rangle</math> is exactly <math>\mathfrak{g}_\nu</math>.

(iii) The bilinear form <math>\langle \nu, [\cdot, \cdot] \rangle</math> on <math>\mathfrak{g}</math> is invariant under <math>G_\nu</math>.

<math>\omega</math> is also [[Closed and exact differential forms|closed]]. The canonical [[2-form]] <math>\omega</math> is sometimes referred to as the ''Kirillov-Kostant-Souriau symplectic form'' or ''KKS form'' on the coadjoint orbit.

===Properties of coadjoint orbits===
The coadjoint action on a coadjoint orbit <math>(\mathcal{O}_\mu, \omega)</math> is a [[Hamiltonian action|Hamiltonian <math>G</math>-action]] with [[momentum map]] given by the inclusion <math>\mathcal{O}_\mu \hookrightarrow \mathfrak{g}^*</math>.
